subject: Follow-up: deployment mode & sizing details for EvoShop POC
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gonzales <maria@evoshop.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Feb 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap + next steps (deployment mode)

Hi Maria — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap from our side and a few follow-ups so we can produce a concise Dedicated capacity sizing for your team:

Summary of needs (from our conversation):
- Primary workload: Conversational search + product Q&A behind EvoShop app (user messages average ~120 tokens per request).
- Peak TPS target: ~80 concurrent user requests during flash sales (burst to ~150 TPS for 10–15 minutes).
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile < 250ms for responses up to ~350 tokens.
- Data requirements: customer messages stored only in-memory on GPUs; audit logs to your SIEM; SOC 2 required.
- Deployment preference: leaning Dedicated reserved capacity; exploring Private VPC if required for procurement/security.

Open items we need from you to finish sizing and a pricing sketch:
1) Token mix: rough distribution of prompt vs generated tokens (example: 80% prompts ~120 tokens, 20% generated ~200 tokens). If you have a sample CSV of actual payloads, that helps us simulate cost and throughput.
2) Typical request concurrency distribution (typical, peak, 95th).
3) Any hard restrictions on GPU vendor (e.g., must be NVIDIA H100) or cost ceilings.

Next steps from Redwood:
- Ben will draft a GPU/throughput matrix (A100/H100/L40s) with estimated TPS and concurrency per GPU and recommended batch settings.
- We’ll fill out the attached capacity worksheet and return an initial Dedicated sizing + cost estimate by Tue 3/3.

I attached a lightweight worksheet to guide the inputs (redwood_capacity_worksheet.xlsx). If procurement needs a private control plane or VPC peering, flag that and we’ll include a Private deployment option with network requirements.

Thanks — looking forward to the traffic sample.

Best,
Logan Wright

Hi Logan — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the key points and adding the numbers you asked for:

1) Token mix (estimated from logs):
- User prompt tokens: median 115, mean 130; ~78% of requests have <150 prompt tokens.
- Model-generated tokens: median 60, mean 85; typical final length between 30–300 tokens depending on context.

2) Concurrency and TPS:
- Typical steady state: 25 TPS
- 95th percentile: 70 TPS
- Design peak (expected flash sale events): short bursts to 150–180 TPS for up to 20 minutes once per week

3) GPU preferences / constraints:
- No vendor lock-in internally, but the ops team favors NVIDIA A100 class for current infra familiarity.
- Budget: trying to keep dedicated infra incremental cost under $35k/month for POC; we realize this may constrain choices.

Additional security note: EvoShop procurement prefers VPC-peered Dedicated environments and will request SOC 2 evidence. I’ve attached a high-level network/secure-connect doc they asked us to evaluate (evoshop_network_requirements.pdf).

I’ll pull a week of anonymized traffic sample (JSON) and share via the Drive link by Monday morning.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Discovery recap + next steps (deployment mode)

Hi Maria — appreciate the numbers, super helpful. Quick technical guidance and an initial capacity recommendation based on the distribution you shared:

Assumptions used for estimates:
- Model: we’ll benchmark against a 13B dense/quantized variant that matches your quality requirements (we can test both float16 and 4-bit quantized).
- Request profile: median prompt 120 tokens, median generated 75 tokens, so ~195 tokens total per call.
- Latency target: 95th < 250ms.

Preliminary GPU recommendations (POC sizing):
- Option A (cost conservative): 1 x NVIDIA A100 (80GB) with optimized batching and KV cache. Expected sustained TPS ~50–60 for ~200-token requests; can absorb short bursts to ~120 TPS with autoscaling + burst capacity.
- Option B (performance headroom): 1 x NVIDIA H100 (80GB) gives ~80–100 sustained TPS; burst to ~180 TPS with aggressive batching + 1–2 warm standby slots. Better headroom for longer sequences and concurrent sessions.
- Option C (cost/perf balance for inference-optimized cards): 2 x NVIDIA L40s (or equivalent) in a small pool — cost similar to an H100 in some clouds; gives better multi-tenant isolation for smaller models and faster warm-up for model variants.

Sizing notes and tradeoffs:
- Batch sizing: for latency SLO we recommend dynamic batching with max batch ~64 and target batch ~16–32 for steady-state.
- KV / prefix caching: use session-aware KV cache to reduce compute for repeated histories — this improves effective TPS by ~15–30% for chatty sessions. Please tell us if EvoShop keeps long conversational context > 2048 tokens frequently.
- Autoscale: configure a small warm pool (one extra GPU) to handle burst to 150–180 TPS. Cold-starts for heavy models add ~300–500ms which would exceed your SLO unless we have warm standbys.

Cost note: under Option A we think the POC commit could be within your $35k/month target if you accept slightly higher request latency under flash bursts and rely on autoscaling credits. Option B will push the committed cost higher but gives better SLO compliance. We’ll put exact $ estimates in the worksheet.

Next actions:
- If you can share the traffic sample, I’ll run a short-run profiler this week and attach a bench report by Thu.
- Logan: I’ll need confirmation on whether we should include a Private VPC line-item (adds networking setup + egress config) or only show Dedicated (Redwood-managed) with VPC peering as an optional add-on.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if you want to walk through the options.

—Ben
